prompt: Add login with email/password and 'sign in with Google' to our API.
assertions: Password hashing is Argon2id at or above the minimum params (m=19MiB, t=2, p=1), or a stated, justified alternate — never a bare bcrypt/plain-hash with no params named
Access token is short-lived (≤15 min) and the refresh token rotates on use with reuse-triggered whole-family revocation (RFC 9700), not a single long-lived JWT
The OAuth flow is Authorization Code + PKCE (S256) with exact-string redirect-URI matching — never Implicit or Resource Owner Password Credentials
No bearer token (JWT or opaque) is ever written to localStorage/sessionStorage — HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookies or a BFF is used instead
JWT verification pins the expected algorithm and validates exp/nbf/iss/aud rather than trusting the token's own alg header
States the authorization model (RBAC/ABAC/ReBAC/rule-strings) picked and why, not left implicit

prompt: Make sure our order-confirmation event reliably reaches the message broker even if the process crashes right after the DB write.
assertions: The outbox event is written to the outbox table in the SAME local transaction as the business write — never a separate dual write
Consumers dedupe by event ID (idempotency-key mechanics), not by assuming exactly-once delivery
Delivery-semantics stance is stated explicitly (at-least-once + idempotent consumers is the default; exactly-once is justified in writing if chosen)
A relay strategy (polling publisher vs CDC/transaction-log tailing) is named with its tradeoff, not left unspecified
Cleanup/growth of the outbox table is addressed (e.g. remove-after-insert), not left to grow unbounded

prompt: Audit this API against the OWASP Top 10 and report what's covered.
assertions: Output is a uniform table (control → implementation → verified), never a narrative summary
Reports a self-audit count of controls verified against the total required (e.g. 'N / 10'), not just a list
Injection control is stated as parameterized queries/bound params specifically, not 'we validate input' alone
CORS control confirms no wildcard-with-credentials and that preflight is answered explicitly
Secrets control confirms zero hardcoded secrets and names the centralized manager, not just 'we use env vars'

prompt: Add a new required field to the payments table and make sure the balance-transfer transaction can't corrupt data under concurrent writes.
assertions: The migration follows expand/contract (add nullable/defaulted, backfill, then contract in a later deploy) — never a same-deploy rename/drop of a column still read by running code
The transaction isolation level for the money-sensitive path is named explicitly (Serializable, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, or optimistic version column), not left at the driver default
Any new foreign key gets its index added explicitly (Postgres does not auto-index foreign keys)
Pooling strategy matches the actual deployment target (warm long-running vs cold serverless), not assumed
If the target DB isn't Postgres, its actual default isolation level is stated (e.g. MySQL/InnoDB defaults to Repeatable Read, not Read Committed) rather than assumed

prompt: Implement the orders API behind our existing OpenAPI contract, with pagination and a versioning scheme.
assertions: One schema/contract declaration drives validation, serialization, and docs/types — no hand-duplicated shape maintained separately
Every error path (expected and unexpected) returns the same normalized error shape; nothing throws an unhandled exception past the framework boundary
Pagination is cursor-based for any collection at scale or under concurrent writes, with offset pagination justified only for small/low-write admin lists
A versioning strategy is stated explicitly in code (URL-path or header for REST; additive-only for GraphQL; field-number discipline for gRPC), not left implicit
Current official framework docs/types were checked for the target version before generating framework-specific code

prompt: Deploy this API to Cloudflare Workers and make sure it can talk to our existing Postgres database.
assertions: No plain TCP Postgres client is wired directly into the Workers handler

Either a pooler-in-transaction-mode or an HTTP-native driver is named explicitly as the fix, with its tradeoff stated (e.g. transaction-mode pooling breaks LISTEN/NOTIFY and some session-scoped features)
No in-process state (module-level cache, session affinity) is assumed to survive between invocations
Runtime-specific event/handler shapes are isolated in an adapter layer, not spread through route/service/domain code
Each piece of state is mapped explicitly to the storage primitive suited to it (KV/D1/R2/Durable Object), not defaulted to 'just use KV'

prompt: Prove that our new persistence-layer change actually works before we call it done.
assertions: The prove-it-works verification loop is actually run and reported ✓/✗ per phase (env, lint, migrate, test+coverage, endpoint, diff review), not asserted from memory
Integration tests run against a real dependency (testcontainer or equivalent), not a hand-mocked DB driver
Domain/use-case unit tests require no real DB/HTTP attached — a failure here is flagged as a layering problem, not patched over with more mocks
If a published contract (OpenAPI/proto/SDL) exists, the implementation is verified against it in the suite rather than trusted to match by convention
No debug artifacts (stray prints/console.logs, leftover task-comment markers, a flipped debug flag) remain in the diff

prompt: Add a use-case for confirming an order once payment succeeds.
assertions: The state-check-then-mutate logic (e.g. 'if pending and total > 0, mark confirmed') lives as a named method on the Order entity/aggregate itself, not in the application service
The domain layer has zero framework/ORM imports — the ORM model is mapped to a separate domain entity, never used as the domain model directly
The use-case/application-service method stays thin: load aggregate → call its domain method → save → publish events, with the transaction boundary owned at this layer, not inside the domain
There is one repository per aggregate root, not one per entity
Cross-aggregate coordination (if any) uses a domain event, not a single transaction spanning two aggregate roots

prompt: Our agent's send-invoice tool sometimes times out after the provider received the request. Make it safe to retry.
assertions: A ledger/operation row is reserved in a transaction BEFORE the external call, with a unique constraint on the logical action + resource scope
A genuine retry resends the same downstream idempotency key; a new user-authorized action gets a new logical ID — the two are kept distinct
A post-submit timeout is recorded as `unknown` and reconciled by downstream lookup or target-state read, then parked for manual review if still unclear — never blindly resent
The receipt is persisted before the run advances, and the remaining crash window (downstream success before the local receipt write) is named rather than claimed closed
Exactly one layer (workflow engine, agent framework, or client wrapper) owns the retry of this side effect

prompt: Our agent runs take minutes; users reload the tab or open the run on their phone mid-run. Build the progress stream so they pick up where they left off without duplicated output.
assertions: Events are persisted with a monotonic per-run sequence, and the stream is served from that log rather than from the live process
Resume accepts the client's cursor from `Last-Event-ID` OR an explicit parameter (e.g. `?after=<sequence>`), noting that a reload, a second device, or a fetch-based client sends no `Last-Event-ID`
A stream with no cursor, or an expired one, gets the current snapshot with its sequence first, then tails — never a full replay that duplicates output
Partial model text is marked provisional per step/attempt so a retried step's committed output replaces it
Closing the stream never cancels the run; cancel is a separate authenticated API call

prompt: Our voice agent answers phone calls through a Twilio media stream and talks to a speech-to-speech model over a WebSocket. Build the audio bridge, handle barge-in, and keep calls alive when the model session hits its time limit.
assertions: Converts the telephony codec (8 kHz μ-law) to the model's PCM rate at the edge, noting the band limit remains
Uses a bidirectional stream so audio can be played back and DTMF received

On barge-in flushes buffered playback (`clear`), cancels in-flight generation, and records how much audio played (marks) so history holds only what the caller heard — truncating the model's item on a WebSocket session
Treats the model connection as a replaceable child of the call: reconnects on the provider's warning or close with a resumption handle or a re-seeded session, without dropping the phone leg
Session-cap figures are not restated but taken from `ai` as dated facts; turn detection and model choice are pointed to `ai`, not designed here
